topic: K-Stick and the Eraser That Erases the Wrong Thing
hook_text: Why did his face just disappear?!
background: Simple classroom or desk backdrop with a reusable whiteboard and small table
main_expression: Wide shocked eyes, then confused blinking, then an embarrassed grin
main_pose: Standing beside the table, holding a pencil in one hand and an eraser in the other
prop: Whiteboard, pencil, and small pink eraser
scene_1: K-Stick proudly writes "I AM A GENIUS" on the whiteboard and poses beside it.
scene_2: He notices a spelling mistake, quickly grabs the eraser, and rubs the word while looking very confident.
scene_3: The words vanish, but so does K-Stick's round white face, leaving only his eyes floating above his stick body.
twist_ending: K-Stick panics, then flips the eraser over and discovers his own face drawn on it. He puts the eraser on his head like a tiny second face and proudly writes, "STILL A GENIUS."
facebook_caption: K-Stick tried to fix one tiny mistake... and erased his whole face instead! 😂✏️
youtube_description: K-Stick grabs an eraser to fix a spelling mistake, but the eraser has a much bigger plan. A quick, family-friendly stickman comedy reel with a silly twist ending.
image_prompt: A clean minimalist 2D cartoon frame featuring K-Stick, a simple black stickman with a round white face, big expressive eyes, and a signature red cap, standing beside a small classroom table and whiteboard. He holds a pencil and pink eraser. Bold readable shapes, flat colors, thick black outlines, white and light-blue background, no copyrighted characters, no crowd, reusable simple props.
motion_prompt: 15-second fast-paced 2D stickman animation. Scene 1: K-Stick proudly writes on the whiteboard and poses. Scene 2: he spots a spelling mistake, grabs the pink eraser, and rubs rapidly with confident exaggerated motion. Scene 3: the writing disappears, then his round white face disappears too, leaving his eyes floating above his body. He blinks in panic, flips the eraser to reveal a tiny drawing of his face, places it on his head, grins, and writes a new punchline on the board. Use snappy timing, simple reusable animation, expressive eye movements, and a cheerful pop sound for the twist.
